subject: Interactive chat latency — customer advisory and client-side mitigations
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastretail.com>, support@fastretail.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Interactive chat latency — initial detection and immediate workarounds

Hi Jordan,

I wanted to let you know we detected intermittent high tail latency impacting streamed/chat responses for accounts routed through our us-west-2 cluster starting ~08:40 PST. Some customer sessions saw chunk gaps of 6–12s before the next token arrived; overall success rate remained high but the user experience degraded.

What we are doing now (high level):
- We have isolated a subset of inference worker hosts showing elevated token emission jitter tied to a kernel selection fallback under heavy concurrent streams.
- Engineering has activated an emergency routing policy to divert new streams away from the affected shard and started a rapid canary of an alternate kernel.
- We're collecting a full trace bundle and request-level logs; attaching a condensed log bundle for your reference (perf_trace_20260302.tar.gz).

Immediate client-side workarounds you can apply while we stabilize (non-breaking, fast):
1) Enable polling fallback: if your client supports it, set streaming_timeout_ms=2000 to close very long waits and poll for remaining tokens instead of blocking the UI.
2) Reduce max_chunk_size to 512 tokens to reduce per-chunk processing pressure.
3) Add simple client-side retry with jitter for chunk timeouts (backoff starting at 500ms, cap 5 retries).
4) As a short-term reliability measure, consider temporarily requesting the non-streamed (complete) response model for very high priority paths — we can route those to a stable pool.

I'll follow up with a consolidated mitigation plan and expected ETA for full recovery. If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the exact client config changes; I can be available in the next hour.

Thanks for the quick heads-up yesterday about the customer session logs — those helped speed diagnosis.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive chat latency — initial detection and immediate workarounds

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the quick notification.

Impact notes from our side:
- We saw an uptick in support tickets starting at ~08:50. Most users were in product search flows; a few sessions timed out in our UI after ~10s.
- Are you able to confirm whether routing to another region (eu-west-1) would immediately avoid the affected hosts? Latency to eu-west-1 is higher but might be acceptable for low-volume admin users.

We can implement the client retry pattern this morning, but would prefer to avoid switching to non-streamed responses unless asked — that will require a client deploy.

If you have a direct point for an exec-level update for our stakeholders, please include it; they will want to know the ETA for stable streaming.

— Jordan
Head of Integrations, FastRetail

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Interactive chat latency — initial detection and immediate workarounds

Team — forwarding FastRetail thread. Key asks: durable customer workaround + short ETA for canary fix.

Notes / triage so far:
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel-selection fallback under sustained concurrent streaming loads triggered use of a slow path in the attention kernel for models with long context; this increases per-token variance and creates large inter-chunk gaps.
- Affected shard: us-west-2-infer-3 (approx 8 hosts).

Immediate operational actions I recommend (please spin up quick tasks):
1) Start regional diversion: route new interactive sessions for FastRetail to us-west-2-infer-6 (stable pool) and schedule a 10-minute rolling restart of the affected hosts to clear the bad kernel state.
2) Canary alternate kernel: deploy the alternate kernel on 2 hosts and test with realtime synthetic traffic for 15 minutes; if stable, expand.
3) Enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for FastRetail's tenant id to reduce per-request compute. Config snippet attached (client_timeout_patch.diff).
4) Customer-facing: send a short advisory with step-by-step client changes (Evelyn to send) and offer a 30-minute troubleshooting session.

Also: suggest we prepare an SLA credit note pre-approval for this account if recovery exceeds 4 hours — Jordan asked for exec-level visibility.

I'll coordinate the customer call. Marcus, can you take the kernel rollout? Monica, can you own routing changes and the restart window? Rachel, please prepare the cache override and the credit template.

Thanks — Evelyn

[attachment: client_timeout_patch.diff (suggested client settings)]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastretail.com>, support@fastretail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Stabilization complete — recommended client playbook & postmortem link

Hi Jordan — quick update and recommended steps to harden your integration against recurrence.

Status:
- We completed the canary rollout and rolling restart of the affected us-west-2 shard on 2026-03-03 at 14:40 PST. The alternate kernel cleared the per-token jitter; stream latency returned to baseline.
- Engineering continues a full postmortem; preliminary write-up is available here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/postmortems/postmortem_interactive_chat_20260304.md

Customer playbook (apply in order):
1) Client-side: implement a short streaming timeout and controlled poll fallback
   - streaming_timeout_ms = 2000 (closes a waiting stream if no token is received within 2s), then poll for remaining output.
   - retry_on_chunk_timeout = true, retry_backoff_ms = [500, 1000, 2000], max_retries = 3.
2) Chunk sizing: request smaller chunks for interactive flows (max_chunk_tokens = 512).
3) Prioritize critical flows: mark high-priority requests to be routed to the stable pool (we set up a tenant override for FastRetail).
4) Telemetry: add event logging for token-gap > 1500ms so we can detect regressions quickly. We can share a lightweight telemetry snippet to add to your integration.

We appreciate FastRetail's patience. As discussed with our ops team, we've drafted a goodwill credit for affected sessions if you prefer it in lieu of fast-tracked SLA paperwork — Rachel will share details.

If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute joint runbook session to apply the client patch and validate in staging; Marcus and I can join tomorrow morning.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

— Jordan
